I'd prefer some other means of attaching the receiver to the stock - the pipe walls are too thin for threaded holes that will be resisting 12 gauge recoil. Also, the safety is not a good design - it was compromised by doubling as a barrel-hold device. A simple bent-pin inserted through the reciever could better be used to positively prevent the barrel from coming all the way back. Tie a string from the pin and loop it over a fixed point on the barrel, ahead of the receiver, and you have your barrel hold as well. That fixed point might be a made from a 1/2 inch section of receiver pipe, glued into place.

The use of the stock as a fallback in case of endcap failure is a good idea, and it would work better if it was snugged up tight against it. You don't want the metal to start moving before trying to stop it. A single, long thick reinforcement bolt, right through the center of the wood, is the strongest way to keep this fallback intact.
